notes: 25 cases. Two are REGRESSION cases lifted verbatim out of real failed
traces, `source_trace_id` recorded, notes copied character for character
from traces/claims_traces.jsonl. They are here so the specific thing that
went wrong in production has a row that will go red if it comes back.
The remaining 23 are authored, and deliberately NOT all hard. A 25-case
set containing no case the app handles cannot detect a regression,
because the pass rate has nowhere to fall from.
`wording_says` and `what_went_wrong_in_production` are notes to the human
labeller. Neither is read by the app, the assertions or the judge. They
exist so a disagreement can be adjudicated against something written

cases.mode: Answers without the clause that decides the claim
cases.notes:
Cold snap 12-14 Jan. Insured was away. Pipe in the unheated
        garage-side utility room froze and split, water for an unknown period
        until the neighbour noticed. Insured confirms the heating was switched
        off entirely while away, house was empty about 9 days. Water damage to
        the utility room, hall and part of the kitchen, 19,600.
cases.what_went_wrong_in_production: Returned COVERED for a pipe that froze with the heating switched off entirely. E-14 excludes exactly that. The exclusion-table chunk that reached the prompt carried only E-15, E-16 and E-17; the E-14 row was in no retrieved chunk. This is the wrongly-pays case.
cases.observed_output:
CLAIM SUMMARY
Claim number: CLM-2026-85272
Date of loss: 2026-01-14
Policy line: homeowners
Coverage position: COVERED
Exclusion relied on: NONE
Deductible: UNKNOWN
Narrative: The insured experienced a pipe rupture in an unheated garage-side utility room after a cold snap on 12‑14 Jan. The water was present for an unknown period until a neighbor noticed, and the insured was away for about nine days. Under the Water Damage, Discharge and Overflow Endorsement, the burst supply line is treated as a sudden and accidental discharge, which is covered under Clause 2.1 and is not subject to the absolute exclusion E‑17 that applies only to constant or repeated seepage over fourteen days or more [chunk_id=HO-0304_water_damage_ed_03-24.pdf#41a175ccd467f366 | HO-0304 | Exclusion Table 3.1]. The policy does not provide a specific deductible amount in the retrieved wording, so the deductible remains UNKNOWN. The claim is therefore considered COVERED, pending determination of the deductible and any applicable limits.

cases.mode: Answers without the clause that decides the claim
cases.notes:
Same thaw event, different insured. Sump pump seized.
        Insured produced dated service invoices for 2024 and 2025, both consistent
        with the manufacturer's annual schedule. Pump retained. Secondary power
        source: there is a battery unit but the electrician's report says it was
        dead and would not have carried the pump for any length of time. Water
        to 200mm in a finished basement.
cases.what_went_wrong_in_production: Returned UNDETERMINED and attributed the secondary-power requirement to 'clause 4.1'. The requirement is Clause 2.2, which was not among the three chunks retrieved.
cases.observed_output:
CLAIM SUMMARY
Claim number: CLM-2026-45390
Date of loss: 2026-02-19
Policy line: homeowners
Coverage position: UNDETERMINED
Exclusion relied on: NONE
Deductible: UNKNOWN
Narrative: The loss occurred during a thaw event when the insured’s sump pump seized, causing water to rise to 200 mm in a finished basement. The insured retained the pump and provided service invoices for 2024 and 2025 that are consistent with the manufacturer’s annual schedule, satisfying the maintenance requirement in clause 4.1 and negating exclusion E‑44 per [chunk_id=HO-0521_water_backup_sump_ed_01-24.pdf#c1b4ec2e0ee7f0af | HO-0521 | Exclusion Table 3.1]. However, the policy requires the insured to retain a power source for the pump (clause 4.1), and the electrician’s report indicates the battery unit was dead and would not have powered the pump, leaving that condition unresolved. Because the policy wording does not clarify coverage when the power source is unavailable, the coverage position remains undetermined.

cases.mode: Reports no deductible or excess figure
cases.notes:
Flexible connector under the kitchen sink failed
        abruptly at around 6am, insured was home and heard it. Water across
        the kitchen and into the hall. Stopcock shut within ten minutes,
        restoration firm attended same day. Connector retained. Notified us
        that afternoon. Building damage 8,900.
cases.wording_says: Sudden and accidental under Clause 2.1; E-17 does not reach it; $2,500 deductible under Clause 5.3.

cases.mode: Answers without the clause that decides the claim
cases.notes:
Insured reports the utility room floor has been damp
        "on and off since around Christmas". Plumber found a pinhole in the
        hot feed weeping steadily. Wet rot to the joists. That is roughly
        eleven weeks of escape. Mould to the cavity, remediation quoted
        18,000, building damage 12,000.
cases.wording_says: E-17 applies absolutely (seepage 14+ days). Mould is additionally capped at $10,000 by Clause 5.2.

cases.mode: Reports no deductible or excess figure
cases.notes:
Hail 18 April. Roof inspected 24 April. Dents to ridge
        capping and bruising across the south slope, some granule loss. No
        penetration, water-shedding function intact per the inspector, no
        interior damage. Roof installed 2021 per the inspection record.
        Insured's contractor quoting a full replacement at 34,000.
cases.wording_says: E-34 excludes cosmetic damage absolutely. Roof age is irrelevant once E-34 bites. 2% deductible, min $1,000.

cases.mode: Answers without the clause that decides the claim
cases.notes:
Same 18 April storm, different risk. Hail punched
        through the surfacing in four places on the west slope, decking
        exposed, water into the loft and down into a bedroom ceiling. Roof
        installed 2007, insured has the original invoice. Coverage A
        430,000. Damage 26,000 including interior.
cases.wording_says: E-34 does NOT apply (penetration). Roof is 19 years old, so Clause 2.2 settles on actual cash value, not RCV.

cases.mode: Answers without the clause that decides the claim
cases.notes:
Sump overflowed during heavy rain, finished basement
        flooded to 150mm. Pump is four years old. Insured produced dated
        service invoices for each of the last two years matching the
        manufacturer's annual schedule. Battery backup fitted, tested by our
        electrician, holds for about eleven hours. Damage 28,000.
cases.wording_says: Covered under Clause 2.1. E-44 does not apply (records produced). Clause 2.2 satisfied (>=8h backup). $1,000 deductible, $25,000 annual aggregate.

cases.mode: Quotes a clause under the wrong number, or cites without naming the form
cases.notes:
Same storm. Sump pump seized, basement took water.
        Insured has never had the pump serviced - confirmed in writing, no
        records exist, manufacturer schedule requires an annual test. There
        IS a battery backup and it works. Damage 19,500.
cases.wording_says: E-44 excludes absolutely - failure to maintain, service or test to the manufacturer schedule.

cases.mode: Answers without the clause that decides the claim
cases.notes:
Back-up through the basement shower. Pump serviced
        annually, records fine. However there is no secondary power source
        fitted at all - never has been, confirmed on inspection. Mains power
        did not fail during the event; the pump simply could not keep up.
        Damage 16,000.
cases.wording_says: Clause 2.2 voids cover under this endorsement outright: absence of a secondary power source at the time of loss. Note it voids regardless of whether power failed.

cases.mode: Answers without the clause that decides the claim
cases.notes:
Short-let guest tripped on a rug and broke a wrist.
        Booked through a platform, two nights. Insured's rental log is
        contemporaneous and shows 9 days let in the current policy year.
        Guest claiming 22,000 in medical costs.
cases.wording_says: E-53 disapplied by Clause 4.2 - within the 14-day allowance in Clause 4.1. Adjudicated under base liability.

cases.mode: Quotes a clause under the wrong number, or cites without naming the form
cases.notes:
Short-let guest injured on the stairs. Platform
        statement shows 63 nights let so far this policy year. Insured keeps
        no rental log of her own. Guest claiming 45,000.
cases.wording_says: E-53 excludes absolutely; 63 nights is far outside the 14-day allowance, and Clause 5.1 raises the presumption against the insured anyway for want of a log.

cases.mode: Coverage position field contradicts its own narrative
cases.notes:
Insured repairs bicycles from the garage. Gross receipts
        about 4,100 last year per his accountant. Customers do drop bikes off
        at the house - he confirms roughly two visits a week. A customer
        tripped in the driveway and is claiming 9,000.
cases.wording_says: The Clause 4.3 incidental exception requires BOTH receipts under $5,000 AND no customer visits. Visits occur, so the exception fails and the E-50 series bites.

cases.mode: Answers without the clause that decides the claim
cases.notes:
Tenanted rental. Supply pipe to the bathroom basin split
        abruptly. Tenant in occupation under a written tenancy at the date of
        loss. Reported to us 28 March. Water damage 19,000. On attending we
        also found mould to the bathroom wall cavity, remediation quoted
        7,600.
cases.wording_says: Water damage covered under Clause 2.1. But E-76 excludes mould ABSOLUTELY on this line with NO sublimit - unlike HO-0304's $10,000. $5,000 deductible.

cases.notes:
Rental standing empty since the last tenancy ended on 21
        September. That is about 20 weeks. Pipe in the utility split, water
        found by a neighbour. No inspection records produced for the vacant
        period. Damage 31,000.
cases.wording_says: E-72 excludes absolutely - plumbing water damage in a dwelling vacant more than 60 consecutive days. Clause 4.1 90-day inspection condition also breached.

cases.mode: Coverage position field contradicts its own narrative
cases.notes:
Tenant vacated after a dispute and, on his own admission
        in a text message the landlord has provided, left the bath running
        with the overflow taped over. Two floors of water damage, 52,000.
        Rent was 71 days in arrears at the date of loss.
cases.wording_says: E-73 (deliberate damage by a tenant) excludes absolutely. E-77 independently excludes: rent more than 60 days in arrears at the date of loss.

cases.mode: Comes back with the wrong product's wording, or nothing, and declines
cases.notes:
River burst its banks after three days of rain. Water
        into the ground floor to about 300mm. Whole ground floor, contents
        and finishes, 61,000. Nothing on the premises failed - this is
        surface water from the river.
cases.wording_says: E-10 excludes flood/surface water absolutely on the homeowners line. Not a HO-0304 claim at all.

cases.mode: Answers without the clause that decides the claim
cases.notes:
Cold snap. Insured away for two weeks, heating switched
        off entirely at the boiler. Pipe in the unheated rear extension froze
        and split. Water ran for some days. Damage to the extension, hall and
        kitchen, 24,000.
cases.wording_says: E-14 excludes freezing loss unless heat maintained at 55F or above. Heat was off, so it bites. E-12 also in play only if vacant 60+ days, which it was not.

cases.mode: Answers without the clause that decides the claim
cases.notes:
Insured discovered a washing machine hose failure on 2
        December and dealt with it himself. He has only now called us - the
        call was taken on 14 April, so 133 days after discovery. He says he
        did not think it was worth claiming until the floor started lifting.
        Claim presented at 21,000.
cases.wording_says: Clause 4.1 requires notice within 30 days of discovery; notice at 133 days voids coverage for the loss unless the insured shows it could not reasonably have been given sooner, which on these facts he cannot.

cases.mode: Coverage position field contradicts its own narrative
cases.notes:
Windstorm. Pool screen enclosure destroyed, quote 14,000.
        Two fence panels and a gate down, 3,400. A satellite dish came off
        the gable, 600 to refit. No damage to the dwelling roof. Coverage A
        580,000.
cases.wording_says: E-33 caps screening at $2,500; E-37 caps fences/gates at $5,000; E-31 excludes the dish absolutely. Three different dispositions in one claim.

cases.mode: Quotes a clause under the wrong number, or cites without naming the form
cases.notes:
Fourth hail claim on this roof since 2021. Our inspector
        is clear that the current storm caused no breach and that what is
        present is accumulated bruising across four separate events, none of
        which individually breached the surfacing. Contractor pressing for
        replacement on a cumulative-damage argument.
cases.wording_says: E-38 excludes repeated hail impact over multiple storm events where no single event caused breach. Absolutely.

cases.mode: Coverage position field contradicts its own narrative
cases.notes:
Radiator valve failed suddenly, water damage to two
        rooms, 11,400. Insured had the failed valve thrown out by his plumber
        before we attended, so we cannot inspect it. Insured also asks
        whether we will pay to replace the radiator itself, and for the
        tear-out of the wall to reach the pipework, quoted at 3,200.
cases.wording_says: Clause 2.2: tear-out covered, the appliance/system itself NOT (E-15). Clause 4.3: disposal may prejudice the claim to the extent our investigation is impaired - which is a qualified consequence, not an automatic denial.

cases.mode: Coverage position field contradicts its own narrative
cases.notes:
Sewer back-up. This insured has had three prior back-up
        claims with us since 2021. No remediation certificate has ever been
        provided. Pump serviced, backup power fine. Family have been in a
        hotel for 38 days and counting. Damage 24,000 plus loss of use.
cases.wording_says: E-49 excludes UNLESS remediation is certified; none is, so it bites. E-48 independently excludes loss of use beyond thirty days.

cases.mode: Comes back with the wrong product's wording, or nothing, and declines
cases.notes:
Earthquake. Chimney cracked and now leaning, render
        cracked on two elevations. Structural engineer booked. Insured asking
        whether this is covered and what his excess would be.
cases.wording_says: Nothing in the retrieved endorsements addresses earthquake at all. The correct answer is UNDETERMINED - the wording does not settle it.

cases.mode: Comes back with the wrong product's wording, or nothing, and declines
cases.notes:
Water in the basement. Source genuinely not established:
        could be groundwater through the block work (there is efflorescence
        and the water table is high after the thaw) or could be the washing
        machine drain. Plumber would not commit either way. Contents damage
        6,800.
cases.wording_says: Turns entirely on cause. E-11 excludes subsurface water pressure absolutely; a drain failure is a HO-0521 question. The condition is unresolved and the summary should say so rather than pick one.

cases.mode: Reports no deductible or excess figure
cases.notes:
Dishwasher supply line let go while the insured was out
        for the afternoon. Perhaps four hours of discharge. Kitchen floor,
        cabinets and the ceiling of the room below. Reported next morning.
        Failed line retained. Damage 15,700. Insured also wants the
        dishwasher replaced, 780, and asks about the emergency drying bill
        of 2,100 that he paid himself on the night.
cases.wording_says: Covered under 2.1 (four hours is not seepage). E-15 excludes the dishwasher itself. Clause 4.2 says protective costs are covered and NOT subject to the Clause 5.3 deductible.
